assessments.reasoning: The six verified publisher slices identify the covered material and forms and preserve the conjunction between paragraphs (a) and (b). Paragraph (b) expressly limits the scope of the alternative sublicense.

challenge.method: Tested an executable sublicense that forbids redistribution of the covered source even though the source is readily available. Separately tested source-rights-preserving terms with no access instructions.
challenge.results: The attempted restriction defeats the paragraph (b) condition without proof of enforcement. In the second case the terms meet that condition, but the missing instructions leave paragraph (a) unsatisfied.

limitations: The permission concerns the executable license. Assessing an actual restriction requires its wording and the source rights it purports to affect.
reasoning: Section 3.2(b) permits MPL terms or a different sublicense for the executable. The condition reaches an attempt by the executable license to alter or limit the recipient's MPL rights in the source. Section 3.2(a) imposes a concurrent source-access duty.
